title: 1960s café racer
reference: 1960s British Triton-style café racer (generic, unbranded): pre-unit 650 vertical parallel twin in a duplex featherbed frame
wheels: Polished alloy-rimmed 40-spoke wire wheels, 19 in front with ribbed tyre and twin-leading-shoe drum (air scoop, linked cam levers), 18 in rear with block tread and single-leading-shoe drum
engine: 650 cc air-cooled OHV pre-unit vertical parallel twin, 3 deg forward, separate four-speed gearbox with primary chaincase, magneto ignition, twin carburettors with chrome bellmouths, swept-back chrome headers into megaphones on both sides, dry-sump oil tank under the seat
colours: British racing green tank (polished alloy lower band), tail cowl and side panels; gloss black frame and swingarm; polished alloy engine cases, oil tank, mudguards, rims and rear-sets; chrome exhaust, fork stanchions and clip-ons; black vinyl seat; smoked flyscreen
weak_points: The featherbed crossover at the head stock is a lug cluster hidden behind the fork and clocks rather than a clearly readable X; the oil tank and battery box are bevelled flat extrusions without seams or straps; the seat is a smooth thin pad without stitching and the tail cowl is not a separate fibreglass shell over the subframe.
